title.text: Distinguish red, yellow and green conditions

why_how.text: A steady circular red signal requires a complete stop before the stop line, crosswalk or intersection.
A No Turn on Red notice prohibits the red-light turn discussed in the handbook's circular-red guidance.
At a flashing red signal, stop completely, yield to crossing traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when clear.
A steady red arrow forbids a turn in its direction until a green or yellow indication permits that movement.
A yellow circular signal warns that the indication is about to become red.
Before entering on a yellow circular signal, a driver should stop when a safe stop is possible.
A driver already in the intersection on a circular yellow should keep moving and clear it safely.
A flashing circular yellow signal calls for slowing, checking carefully for hazards and continuing cautiously.
A solid yellow arrow warns that the turn signal is changing.
Before entering on a solid yellow arrow, a driver should stop if it can be done safely.
A driver already in the intersection on a solid yellow arrow should continue the turn and clear the intersection safely.
A flashing yellow arrow permits a turn only after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians in crosswalks.
A circular green indication allows forward travel.
A driver turning left from a left-turn lane on circular green must first yield to oncoming traffic and crosswalk pedestrians.
Even on a signal allowing movement, a driver should not enter unless there is enough room beyond the intersection for the entire vehicle to clear it.
